title: Israeli airstrike in Beirut kills Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah
body:
On the afternoon of Friday 27 September 2024, Israeli fighter jets struck Beirut's southern suburbs. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said the target was Hezbollah's central headquarters, which it said was embedded under a residential building. On Saturday 28 September the IDF announced that it had killed Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah, and two US officials confirmed his death to CBS News. Hezbollah confirmed the death the same day, saying he had "joined his fellow martyrs."

The IDF said Ali Karki, commander of Hezbollah's Southern Front, was killed along with other commanders. Iranian state media said Gen. Abbas Nilforoushan of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps was also killed. Lebanon's health ministry said at least 11 people were killed and 108 wounded in the Friday strikes, with the toll possibly rising.

The strike came during a week of heavy Israeli bombardment of Lebanon. According to Lebanese Health Ministry statistics, more than 720 people were killed in Lebanon by Israeli strikes that week, and the United Nations said more than 200,000 Lebanese had been displaced in the same period. It followed the pager and walkie-talkie explosions of 17 and 18 September. Israel launched a ground operation in southern Lebanon on 1 October 2024, and Iran fired missiles at Israel the same day, citing the killing of Nasrallah.
